Hook

Top hooks, yt-script score

  • 0In 1999, a 15-year-old downloaded part of the software that helps run the space station's air.
  • 0He hacked NASA and the Pentagon at 15, then emailed them to explain the holes.

Look and device

Running device

A star map of 'systems' (NASA, Pentagon agency) that light up as he gets in, each followed by a polite 'here's your security hole' email card; in the second half a web of string on a corkboard links names in a case he wasn't part of.

Look

Late-90s internet story in the house 2D style, Gumball/t-shirt character style (same as Parts 1-4). Painted plates: a South Florida suburban house, a teen bedroom with a CRT monitor and Star Trek posters, NASA mission-control style room, a Pentagon-style building exterior, an early-morning FBI raid, a juvenile court, a quiet house years later. Calm, warm palette; the ending is gentle, slow and respectful. Real people stylised with no likeness. No hacking method detail. Suicide handled per safe-messaging practice: no method, no details of the note, no framing of it as a solution or as 'regaining control'; helpline card on screen. SFX under the VO (dial-up modem, CRT hum, door knock), music at combine.

Act 1: The Boy at the Computer

0:35 · 4 shots · 86 words
  1. 1.01WIDE9.8s

    AGE 6

Act 2: Just Exploring

0:49 · 5 shots · 120 words
  1. 2.01MED12.8s

    For him it's a challenge, not a heist. He breaks in to prove a system isn't as secure as it thinks. Sometimes he emails the admin afterwards to point out the hole.

    An email card: 'Your setup has holes. Here's where.'

    'HERE'S YOUR HOLE'

    ANIMATIONEmail slides into an inbox.

  2. 2.02MED6.4s

    Summer 1999. He gets into NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Alabama, onto 13 computers.

    A NASA-style control room; 13 screens lighting up one by one.

    13 NASA COMPUTERS

    ANIMATIONScreens light in sequence.

  3. 2.03MED12.1s

    He downloads software NASA valued at 1.7 million dollars, part of the space station's environment controls. He later said the code was poor, and he only wanted to study it.

Fact log

Fixes against the transcript

  • NASA Marshall intrusion June 1999: 13 computers, software valued ~$1.7M, ~21-day shutdown.
  • DTRA (Defense Threat Reduction Agency) server intrusion August 1999.
  • FBI raid January 2000; sentenced September 2000 (house arrest + probation); 6 months detention after probation violation. Described as first juvenile incarcerated for cybercrime in the US.
  • Gonzalez sentenced March 2010 to 20 years; informant for the Secret Service.
  • 'JJ' likely Stephen Watt per later reporting; stated as 'likely someone else'.
  • Jonathan James died 18 May 2008. Safe messaging: no method, no note contents, no weapon, helpline card shown, not framed as a solution.
  • Reel 'Recap' avoids the death; reels on the death excluded.

Removed from the transcript

  • Method of death, weapon and note quotes removed.
  • Wardriving/card-skimming method detail cut.
  • Seinfeld clip and archive news audio cut.
  • Rewritten in our own words.
